summary: Project AstroMeds is an integrated hardware-and-web astronaut health and habitat monitoring system designed for deep-space missions. The physical monitoring device continuously tracks real-time temperature and humidity levels affecting crew members, paired with a synchronized web dashboard that gives astronauts immediate visibility into their own health metrics. Whenever temperature or humidity shifts outside safe physiological thresholds, the system automatically triggers real-time alerts and transmits telemetry back to mission control teams on Earth. By bridging onboard crew self-monitoring with continuous ground-based oversight, Project AstroMeds addresses the critical challenge of maintaining astronaut health and preventing environmental stress during long-duration spaceflight, enabling rapid intervention before minor fluctuations escalate into medical emergencies.
details:
What It Does & How It Works Project AstroMeds is an integrated hardware-and-software medical telemetry and medication management system designed for deep-space missions and isolated environments. Using an Arduino-based hardware unit paired with a real-time web telemetry dashboard ("Crew Terminal"), the system tracks crew health metrics, monitors environmental storage conditions for sensitive pharmaceuticals, and automates dosage scheduling and inventory alerts.

Benefits & Intended Impact In long-duration spaceflight, communication delays with Earth mean astronauts must manage medical emergencies and pharmaceutical stability autonomously. Project AstroMeds reduces human error during high-stress missions by providing instant visual telemetry, preventing medication degradation caused by temperature or radiation fluctuations, and ensuring critical medical supplies are tracked accurately. On Earth, this same low-power telemetry architecture can be adapted for remote clinics and off-grid emergency medical stations.
